rationale:
Issue #148 reports that @DependencyEndpoint emits invalid Swift when the endpoint default uses fatalError, and merged PR #158 ("Fix fatalerror default", body "Fixes #148") targets exactly that expansion defect; traceability is fix_commit -> merged PR -> issue. The retained production hunk relaxes the pre-existing guard `if !functionType.isVoid, closure.statements.count == 1, ...` in DependencyEndpointMacro so the implicit-`return` rewrite also applies to Void endpoints whose single statement is an immediately-invoked closure; without it the generated `_foo` body places `{ fatalError() }()` directly after `XCTestDynamicOverlay.XCTFail(...)`, which parses as a trailing closure rather than valid intended code. The supplied pre-PR baseline evidence (PR base 6c2bbde, blob 742b3ef, merge-base check confirming 6c2bbde is an ancestor of buggy revision 9b56680) shows the `!functionType.isVoid` exclusion existed before the PR branch, so the defect is pre-existing rather than introduced by the selected intra-PR parent. Minimization retained only hunk 2 and dropped the pure-formatting `if\n let initializer` collapse, leaving a single behavioral change with no refactor, feature, doc, or config content; post-minimization strict gates report all checks passed with the single selector Tests/DependenciesMacrosPluginTests/DependencyEndpointMacroTests.swift::testFatalError_SilenceWarning failing on the buggy revision, clean on the fixed revision, deterministic across 3 repetitions, and the full suite green when fixed. The trigger is the project's own assertMacro expansion snapshot for `public var foo: () -> Void = { { fatalError() }() }`, exercising only the pre-existing @DependencyEndpoint macro; no production API is introduced by the fix. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #148 is not a duplicate of any registry entry.

Issue #148 reports that @DependencyEndpoint emits invalid Swift when a default value uses fatalError (the generated unimplemented body lacks a usable return statement). PR #158 ('Fix fatalerror default', 'Fixes #148') contains the selected fix commit cace5f89, and traceability is fix_commit_to_merged_pr_to_issue with verified_fix_issue_numbers=[148]. The retained production hunk in Sources/DependenciesMacrosPlugin/DependencyEndpointMacro.swift relaxes the `!functionType.isVoid` guard so the implicit-return rewrite also applies when the single statement is an immediately-invoked closure, which is the same generated-code-validity defect: without it the expansion emits `XCTFail("Unimplemented: 'foo'")` followed by a bare `{ fatalError() }()` statement. Pre-existence at the PR base is supported by concrete evidence rather than a label: pre_pr_baseline_evidence records merge-base(6c2bbde, 9b56680) == 6c2bbde, base tree 4dbd710, source blob 742b3ef, and quotes the base-revision guard `if !functionType.isVoid, closure.statements.count == 1, ...` at lines 79-83, so the Void-path exclusion that the retained hunk repairs predates the PR branch and was not created by the intra-PR buggy revision 9b56680. Minimization retained only hunk 2 (semantic guard) and dropped hunk 1, which was pure formatting (`if\n let initializer` collapsed onto one line); the minimized production patch therefore has no refactor, feature, docs, config, or test content, and strict_post_minimization passes every gate with the same single reproduced selector. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test edit to the existing testFatalError_SilenceWarning case, switching `foo` from `() -> String` to `() -> Void` plus the matching expansion snapshot; it exercises only the pre-existing @DependencyEndpoint macro and swift-macro-testing assertMacro, introducing no API added by the fix, and the sibling `bar: () -> String` case keeps the non-Void path covered. Machine evidence shows a clean differential (buggy isolated/suite failure limited to that selector, fixed all-green, 3 repetitions, 32-run matrix, deterministic fingerprint groups=3). active_same_project_root_causes is empty and pointfreeco/swift-dependencies#148 is the sole allowed root cause id, so no duplicate exists.
